originalSourceVisualAltDescriptions: A group of dots with 4 rows of 3.
Two triangles. Left, shorter but longer. Right, taller but shorter.
Two ovals. Left, smaller oval. Right, larger oval.
Left, hexagon. Right, triangle. Triangle less than half size of hexagon.
2 rectangles. If cut up, rectangle on right could fit inside rectangle on left.
Top, 6-sided hexagon. Bottom, 8-sided polygon, resembles upside-down heart.
3 shapes. Top, 5-sided polygon, labeled A. Middle, parallelogram ,labeled B. Bottom, rectangle, labeled� C.

learnerSourceCheck.prompt: Compare the source triangles and shape pairs by area rather than apparent height. Explain a method to compare covered space.

supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceGoal: Let’s compare the size of shapes.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceLearningGoals: Describe the relative size of plane figures in their own language.
teachingSteps: Identify the region covered, not only a side length.
Compare using equal-area parts, matching shapes or an overlay.
Explain how you know which covers more or if they cover the same area.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.caution: A larger perimeter, width or visual length alone does not prove a larger area.
